short_description: Tour a real castle built by Tesla's protégé, then explore historic Salem to uncover the truth of the infamous Salem Witch Trials — all in one day.
cancellation_summary: 14+ days prior 100%; 7-14 days prior 50%; no refund within 7 days
meeting_point: Pickup at your hotel in Boston/Cambridge
description: Experience the best of Massachusetts' North Shore in one unforgettable private day trip! Start with a scenic coastal drive to Hammond Castle, a hidden gem most locals have never visited — a medieval-style castle built by eccentric inventor John Hays Hammond Jr., protégé of Tesla and Edison, complete with an 8,000-pipe organ and secret passages. After a guided castle tour, head to Salem for lunch and an afternoon walking tour: the Witch Trials Memorial, the Witch House, Hocus Pocus filming locations, and the grand mansions of Salem's golden age of trade. Castle admission, private vehicle, and hotel pickup are all included.
itinerary:
1. 60 min - Pick Up and Transfer to Hammond Castle Museum
Your guide will pick you up in a comfortable minivan and drive you out to Hammond Castle Museum!

2. 75 min - Hammond Castle Museum
Enjoy a guided tour, learning about the origin and history behind the Castle. You will then have time to explore the rest of the grounds and take photos!

3. 30 min - Transfer to Salem
Drive to Salem for lunch and the afternoon exploration!

4. 60 min - Break
Enjoy an hour for lunch at one of Salem's many excellent restaurants (cost not included)!

5. 15 min - East India Square
Learn about Salem's maritime past and how it became one of the richest cities in America.

6. 20 min - Salem Common
See the heart of historical Salem and learn about the Puritans who settled the town.

7. 25 min - Salem Witch Trials Memorial
Visit the Witch Trials Memorial and learn what really happened in Salem in 1692.

8. 15 min - Old Burying Point Cemetery
See the oldest cemetery in Salem, with graves going back to the Salem Witch Trials.

9. 10 min - Houdini Way
Learn about Harry Houdini's publicized escape from Salem's jail.

10. 10 min - Bewitched Statue
Learn how the famous show Bewitched put Salem on the tourism map!

11. 20 min - The Witch House
The last standing home with direct ties to the 1692 trials. Learn of Judge Jonathan Corwin, who lived here and was one of the examiners of accused "witches", and of his family's connection to Giles Corey's execution, which gave rise to the legendary Corwin Curse.

12. 15 min - Ropes Mansion & Garden
This 1727 Georgian mansion hides a dark past — two members of the Ropes family died tragically here, and locals say their ghosts still roam the property. You may also recognize it as Allison's house from Hocus Pocus.

13. 15 min - Chestnut Street District
Walk Salem's most prestigious street, where sea captains built grand mansions from fortunes earned in the East India spice trade. These homes tell the story of how Salem rivaled Boston as New England's wealthiest port.

14. 5 min - Hamilton Hall
Step up to America's first "red carpet" at this Federal-style hall named for the founding father. Built in 1805, it was the social center of Salem's merchant elite — and it's still used for events today.

15. 15 min - Proctor's Ledge Memorial
See the location where the witches were hanged during the Salem Witch Trials.

16. 30 min - Return to Boston & Drop Off
Your guide will drop you off back at your hotel, cruise ship, or airport terminal!
highlights:
Hammond Castle is the hidden gem even most locals have missed: a genuine medieval-style castle perched on the ocean cliffs of Gloucester, built by the "Father of Radio Control" — a man mentored by Tesla and Edison who loved pranking high-society guests with secret passages and fake ghosts.

In Salem, your guide separates history from Hollywood. Learn who was really accused in 1692 and why the hysteria spread, how none of the victims were burned, and how a judge's family gave rise to the legendary Corwin Curse. You'll also catch Salem's lighter side, from Houdini's jailbreak stunt to the TV show that put the city on the tourism map.

This is the only way to see both in one day without renting a car. The castle sits in Gloucester, nearly an hour outside Boston, and your private vehicle links the coastal drive, the castle, and Salem's walkable center seamlessly.

As a private tour, the day bends to your group. Linger in the castle's great hall, dig deeper into Witch Trials history, or ask your guide to point out every Hocus Pocus filming location — it's your call.
highlight_title: Castles & Curses on the North Shore
highlight_description: Two North Shore legends in one day: a guided tour inside Hammond Castle, then Salem's Witch Trials history — with castle admission, private transportation, and hotel pickup all included.
special_requirements:
Massachusetts law requires proper car seats until children are 8 years old or 57 inches tall. We do not provide car seats, and refunds will not be available day of for lack of proper seating.

Vehicle size does not account for luggage; let us know if you'll need to bring luggage along so we can ensure we have space.
restrictions: Hammond Castle Museum is not handicapped accessible. The castle has multiple levels connected by stairs, uneven stone floors, and narrow passages. We cannot accommodate wheelchairs or strollers at this location and do not recommend this tour if such access is required. The tour includes approximately 3.5 hours of walking.
disclaimers: We run rain or shine unless there is a declared weather emergency. This tour is only available when Hammond Castle is open (typically April through December, with limited winter availability). Due to crowds in Salem, this tour does not run in October.

faq_items.question: When is Hammond Castle open?
faq_items.answer: Hammond Castle Museum is typically open from April through December, with limited availability through the winter. Hours vary, so this tour is only available when the castle is open. Check our booking calendar for current availability. Note that although Hammond Castle is open, due to crowds in Salem, this tour does not run in October — check out our Salem Full-Day Private Trip instead!

faq_items.question: Is this tour suitable for children?
faq_items.answer: Yes! Children of all ages are welcome. The castle's medieval architecture and secret passages fascinate kids, and the Salem stories can be adjusted for younger audiences. Note that Massachusetts law requires proper car seats for children under 8 years old or under 57 inches tall, and we do not provide car seats. Please note: Hammond Castle Museum is not handicapped accessible. We cannot accommodate wheelchairs or strollers at this location.

faq_items.question: Will we see Hocus Pocus filming locations?
faq_items.answer: Yes! We stop at the Ropes Mansion (Allison's house in the movie) and pass by several other filming locations during our walking tour of Salem. Your guide can point out more locations if you're a big fan - just let us know!

faq_items.question: What if it rains?
faq_items.answer: Tours run rain or shine. The Hammond Castle portion is indoors, but about 2 hours of the Salem walking tour is outside with little cover, so dress for the weather. We provide umbrellas, and we recommend comfortable, weather-appropriate shoes.

faq_items.question: Is there a shared tour option?
faq_items.answer: Yes! If you're traveling solo or in a small group and prefer to join others, check out our Castles & Curses: Hammond Castle & Salem Semiprivate Day Trip. It runs on select weekends during the summer season with a maximum of 9 guests.
